title: SLO-aware synthetic workload eval for batching & KV strategy tradeoffs
creator: Jonah Kim
description: Run a set of controlled synthetic workload experiments to quantify latency vs. quality tradeoffs across batching and KV-cache strategies. Deliver a composite SLO risk metric (Sherpa score) that weights p95 latency exposure and quality regression probability for use in rollout guardrails and automated rollback triggers.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Sherpa score implemented in eval harness and reproducible across runs. 2) Matrix of KV-expiry x batch-size x microbatch-profile produced with p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, model-quality delta (BLEU/ROUGE/LLR or model-specific quality metric). 3) Threshold recommendations for runtime-1.19 rollout (safe, caution, unsafe) with documented trade-offs. 4) Playbook entry for console alerts when Sherpa score crosses 'caution' in production slices.
experiment_design:
- Workloads: interactive chat (short-turns), assistant long-form (multi-turn long context), embedding API (bulk small inputs).
- Variables: batch_size (1,4,8,16), microbatch_size (1,2,4), kv_expiry_sec (0,30,120,600), prefix_cache_enable (on/off), tokenization_shard (0/1).
- Metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail QPS, tokens/sec, CPU/GPU utilization, quality delta measured on canonical eval set (delta in LLR+ROUGE for gen models; embedding cosine drift for embed workloads).
- Composite scoring: Sherpa score = weighted combination of normalized p95-exceedance probability and expected quality regression probability; tunable weights to reflect customer SLOs.
- Repeats: 10 runs per cell, seeded RNG for deterministic prompt ordering, collect and store raw traces and KV hit/miss rates.
run_plan: Day 0: finalize canonical eval prompts and slice definitions (sensitive slices: few-shot, long-context, high-perplexity).
Day 1: extend test harness (sherpa-prober) to sweep variables and emit Sherpa score; add new exporters for console traces.
Day 2-3: execute full sweep on staging cluster with runtime-1.19 image; gather traces to GCS and BigQuery-exported summary table.
Day 4: analyze results, identify frontier configs that trade 5-10% latency for <1% quality drop and vice versa.
Day 5: draft recommendations and alert/playbook PRs; present to SRE and PM for signoff.
results_snapshot: Initial micro-run (subset of cells): batch_size=8 + kv_expiry=120s reduced p95 by ~18% but introduced a mean quality drop of 0.9% on assistant long-form slice.
KV hit rate correlated strongly with quality preservation for long contexts; disabling prefix_cache increased latency but preserved per-turn coherence.
Embedding workload showed minimal quality sensitivity to KV expiry but significant throughput gains for batch_size>=16.
Sherpa score prototypes rank configs where Sherpa<0.2 as 'safe', 0.2-0.5 as 'caution', >0.5 as 'unsafe' for our baseline SLO weights (latency-focused).
decisions_and_tradeoffs: Decision: Use Sherpa composite score for rollout guardrails rather than raw quality delta or latency alone — protects against optimizing one metric at the cost of the other.

Tradeoff: Aggressive batching (>=16) yields 2-3x token/sec but can surface subtle degenerations on multi-turn assistants due to KV eviction patterns; recommend conservative batching for assistant workloads.

Tradeoff: Shortening kv_expiry to 30s reduces memory pressure and improves p95 slightly but increases LLR regressions in long-context slices; recommend 120s as default for public hosted tier with option to lower for high-throughput embed-only customers.
next_steps: Finish full sweep across all workload slices on staging (ETA 2026-03-12).
Automate Sherpa score alerting to console and tie to rollout API: if Sherpa>'caution' in >10% of production slices for >15m, trigger canary rollback.
Finalize recommended defaults for runtime-1.19 and prepare runtime release note blurb about KV/batching recommendations.
Schedule cross-functional review with PM (Luis Moreno) and SRE (Emily Zhang) on 2026-03-15.
